# Re-adding an existing node duplicates it in the TreeStore hierarchy

## Context

Surfaced while building #17840 (path materialization), where idempotence is an acceptance criterion. The materializer filters against store state rather than trusting the store to dedupe — this ticket is *why* it has to.

The behaviour is already pinned by a passing CONTROL spec in PR #17854 (`test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStorePathMaterialization.spec.mjs`, "CONTROL: a raw `add()` of the same node DOES duplicate it"). That spec asserts the **current, wrong** behaviour deliberately, so the AC below includes inverting it.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T16:28:32Z, plus a keyword sweep for duplicate/childrenMap/sibling/TreeStore across the latest 60 open; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight sweep: latest 30 messages across all read states — active claims are Brain #215, Engine #17850/#17853, Institution #48/#50, DevIndex #11, Skills #15, #17820/#17838/#17844; none claims src/data/.`

## The Problem

Adding a record whose key already exists corrupts the Structural Layer. The two layers disagree afterwards: the Projection Layer's count is right, the hierarchy's is not.

```javascript
const store = Neo.create(TreeStore, {model: TestModel, data: []});

store.add({id: 'Group', parentId: 'root', name: 'Group', isLeaf: false});
store.add({id: 'Group', parentId: 'root', name: 'Group', isLeaf: false});

store.getCount();                // 1  — correct
store.getChildren('root');       // ['Group', 'Group']  — WRONG
store.get('Group').siblingCount; // 2  — WRONG
```

The ARIA consequence is the part that hurts: `updateSiblingStats` derives `siblingCount` from `siblingMap.length`, so a screen reader is told "1 of 2" for a level that has one node. That is the silent, view-invisible failure class — the tree renders correctly and reports itself incorrectly.

Adding the **same object reference** twice is correctly skipped. Only an equal-but-distinct literal duplicates, which is the ordinary shape for anything re-reading from a config, a fixture, or an API.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.data.TreeStore#splice` ingests additions into the Structural Layer at `src/data/TreeStore.mjs`, in the "Process Additions & Moves" block:

```javascript
me.#allRecordsMap.set(key, data);          // keyed — an existing key is OVERWRITTEN
// …
if (!me.#childrenMap.get(parentId).includes(data)) {   // identity — a new literal is NEVER found
    me.#childrenMap.get(parentId).push(data);
    affectedParents.add(parentId)
}
```

The asymmetry is the defect. `#allRecordsMap` is keyed, so the second add replaces the entry. `#childrenMap` holds arrays and tests membership with `Array#includes`, i.e. by object identity — and the new literal is a different object, so it is appended beside the old one. The children array now holds a **stale object and a live one under the same key**.

`updateSiblingStats` (same file) then counts that array, which is how the wrong value reaches `siblingCount` and `childCount`.

Related asymmetry worth checking in the same pass: the "auto-heal disconnected branches" path in the same block rewrites `data.parentId` to `'root'` when the declared parent is absent, but `depth` was already computed above it — so an auto-healed root node keeps `depth: 1`. Same family (a mutation that does not carry its derived invariants), different symptom, and cheap to fix alongside.

## The Fix

Make the `#childrenMap` membership test key-based rather than identity-based, consistent with `#allRecordsMap` directly above it. When the key is already present in the child array, replace that entry rather than appending — the record is being updated, not added a second time.

Keep the existing same-reference fast path working, and keep `affectedParents` accurate so `updateSiblingStats` still runs when a replacement changes anything it derives.

| `siblingCount` / `siblingIndex` / `childCount` | `src/data/TreeModel.mjs`, `updateSiblingStats` | Unchanged logic; correct once the array it counts is correct | n/a | TreeStore guide | Verified: the fields are derived from `siblingMap.length` |
| `Neo.data.TreeStore#materializePath` | `src/data/TreeStore.mjs` (#17840) | Unaffected — it already filters existing keys before adding | n/a | TreeStore guide | Its idempotence specs pass today against the buggy `splice` |

## Decision Record impact

`none`. No ADR in `learn/agentos/decisions/` governs data-store hierarchy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `add()` of a record whose key already exists leaves `getChildren(parentId)` with exactly one entry for that key.
- [ ] `siblingCount` and `childCount` are unchanged by a re-add that adds no new node.
- [ ] The re-added record's field values win — the stale object does not remain reachable through `getChildren()`.
- [ ] Adding the same object reference twice still no-ops, as it does today.
- [ ] The CONTROL spec in `TreeStorePathMaterialization.spec.mjs` is **inverted** to assert the corrected behaviour, with its comment updated to say what it now pins. It currently documents the defect on purpose; leaving it asserting duplication after the fix would turn a control into a false green.
- [ ] An auto-healed node — one whose declared parent was absent and which `splice` re-parents to `'root'` — carries `depth: 0`, not the depth computed against its absent parent.
- [ ] Unit coverage run via the repo's explicit Playwright configs (`npm run test-unit`), **not** bare `npx playwright test`.

## Out of Scope

- **Path materialization.** #17840 / PR #17854 own that; this ticket is the store-level defect it works around.
- **The silent re-parenting itself.** That an unknown parent heals to `'root'` rather than throwing is existing, intentional-looking behaviour with its own consumers; only its `depth` inconsistency is in scope here.
- **Deletion reconciliation** and any change to `remove()` / descendant cleanup.

## Avoided Traps

**Rejected: "make the materializer own dedup and leave `splice` alone."** It already does, and that is exactly what makes this ticket necessary rather than optional — the workaround lives in one caller while every other `add()` caller stays exposed. A store whose two layers disagree about how many children a node has is a data-layer defect, not a caller concern.

**Trap: fixing the count without fixing the reachable object.** Removing the duplicate array entry while leaving the *stale* one in place would make `siblingCount` correct and `getChildren()` return an object that `get()` no longer returns. Both maps must end up pointing at the same record.

### First, a correction to my own ticket

The **Fix** section names one membership test. There are **two**, and AC-1 needs both:

- [`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1111`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/data/TreeStore.mjs#L1111) — the main path
- [`src/data/TreeStore.mjs:1133`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/src/data/TreeStore.mjs#L1133) — the same identity test inside the auto-heal branch that re-parents an orphan to `'root'`

Both are `!…includes(data)`; both compare by object identity, so an equal-but-distinct literal is never found by either. Fix only the first and a re-added **orphan** still duplicates. That is a gap in my spec — you should not have had to discover it in review.

### Where things live

| | |

| the defect | `src/data/TreeStore.mjs`, the "Process Additions & Moves" block |
| the derived counts | `updateSiblingStats`, same file — no logic change needed, it just counts a corrected array |
| the CONTROL to invert (AC-5) | `test/playwright/unit/data/TreeStorePathMaterialization.spec.mjs:140` |

**On AC-5:** the spec at line 140 asserts the *current, wrong* behaviour on purpose — it was written to pin the bug while a different ticket worked around it. After your fix it must be inverted, comment included. Leaving it as-is would turn a control into a false green.

### Two local gotchas that will bite

1. **Run `npm install` before your first commit.** It registers Husky hooks; without them you'll fail CI on hygiene you never saw locally.
2. **Never put a ticket number in a source comment.** `buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs` gates `src/`, `ai/` and `test/playwright/` and rejects `#12345`, `Epic #N`, `Discussion #N`, `ADR-0019` in comment context. So no `// fixes #17855`. Strings are fine — a ticket ref inside a `describe(...)` title passes. I have tripped this one twice myself.

Also per CONTRIBUTING: **PRs target `dev`**, not `main`.

### A suggested order

Reproduce first — the snippet in the ticket body runs as-is and `getChildren('root')` returning `['Group', 'Group']` is the whole bug. Write the failing test **before** the fix, so you know the test can actually fail. Then both call sites, then invert the CONTROL. The `depth` item (AC-6) is a separate small thing in the same block; take it in the same PR or say so if you'd rather leave it.

Ask anything here — a half-finished PR with a question attached is welcome, and there is no such thing as a question too basic on a ticket labelled `good first issue`. If you decide it isn't for you after all, just say so and I'll unassign; no explanation needed.
